adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Nigeria - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ rights in Nigeria' entry records the national framework that applies in full in Kogi: the Same Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2013, passed by the House of Representatives on 30 May 2013 and signed into law by President Goodluck Jonathan in January 2014, makes entering a same-sex marriage or civil union liable to 14 years' imprisonment and makes registering, operating or participating in 'gay clubs, societies and organisations' or making a public show of a same-sex amorous relationship liable to 10 years' imprisonment. The Criminal Code separately criminalises sex between men with up to 14 years' imprisonment and gross indecency with up to 3 years, while the twelve Shari'a-administering northern states (with death penalties applied in Kano and Katsina for lesbianism) impose harsher penalties, placing non-Shari'a states such as Kogi under the federal 14-year maximum. In 2022 a coalition of Nigerian human rights organisations won a court ruling that Sections 4(1), 5(2) and 5(3) of the 2013 Act breached the Constitution and could not be enforced anywhere in the country, effectively allowing LGBTQ+ organisations and individuals to exist and organise; the entry records no similar ruling for the conduct and marriage-prohibition provisions. It also notes the Constitution has no specific protections for sexual orientation and that there are no federal anti-discrimination protections for LGBTQ people.
